rationale: Four distinct cycles re-derived annotation-over-rewrite while repairing duplicate ADR numbers and a lost cycle file: W0 dedupe placed bracket notes into 0052/0200 declaring record integrity preserved with no silent rewrite; 0052 and 0200 each annotated ADR-0002 to 0007 in place; 1300 discloses its recreation as a recovered record with content unchanged and timestamp preserved. Distinct from L041 (stale truth-lists expire and must be re-derived) and from L011 machine audit chains: this governs how human-facing records are amended without breaking their integrity.

lesson.title: Amend historical records only by dated annotation or disclosed recreation - never silent rewrite
lesson.lesson: Historical records (cycle logs, ADRs, decision papers, ledgers) are corrected only by dated bracket annotations or disclosed recreation. When a duplicate forces a removal or rename, update cross-references AND leave bracket notes in every older record citing the old name. When a file is lost, recreate it marked as a recovered record with content unchanged and timestamp preserved. A reader must always be able to distinguish what was true when written from what was corrected later.
